newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Budget cuts to help rates outlook - Howard.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Budget cuts to help rates outlook - Howard.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Thursday there would be a better prospect of lower interest rates if the opposition passed the government's budget measures in parliament.

"If you were to pass our budget, if you were to stop filibustering on the budget in the Senate, if you were prepared to pass the Workplace Relations Bill, if you were prepared to vote in favour of all the other measures that are designed to achieve fiscal consolidation, then we would have a far greater prospect over time of having even lower interest rates," Howard told parliament.
The Reserve Bank cut official cash rates on Wednesday to 6.5 percent from 7.0 percent, after having reduced rates from 7.5 percent in July.
Howard has said the government's 1996/97 budget, which cuts government spending dramatically, would contribute to downward pressure on interest rates over the long-term.
Treasurer Peter Costello said earlier on Thursday there was room for further rate cuts if inflation and wages growth could be restrained.
